item.title: Rates Rise as Travel and Digital Choices Shift
item.description: Interest rates rise as transport, travel and digital choices shift.
item.content:encoded:
Interest rates rise as transport, travel and digital choices shift.

  1. RBNZ raises the OCR to 2.75% The Reserve Bank raised New Zealand’s Official Cash Rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% on 2 September; ANZ then lifted its Standard Floating home-loan rate to 6.29% and Flexible revolving rate to 6.40%, with its Serious Saver rate due to rise to 2.05% on 1 October. 2 Sep 2026. RBNZ · ANZ rate changes · Follow up
  2. Two Milford Sound quakes close a Queenstown bridge overnight Two shallow earthquakes of magnitude 5.5 and 5.6 struck near Milford Sound less than an hour apart; Queenstown Lakes District Council closed Edith Cavell Bridge near Arthur’s Point overnight pending an engineering inspection. 2 Sep 2026. GeoNet · 1News · Follow up
  3. Nearly 10,000 public servants plan a September 9 strike Nearly 10,000 New Zealand public servants are scheduled to strike for several hours on 9 September across agencies including Internal Affairs, NEMA, Ethnic Communities, MBIE and the Ministry of Social Development. 31 Aug 2026. Reuters · Follow up
  4. Parakai opens a new geothermal wellness experience Kaipātiki Hot Springs officially opened Kaipātiki Ora Restore & Connect, a new premium geothermal wellness experience in Parakai, creating a new bookable hot-springs and relaxation option near Auckland. 2 Sep 2026. Scoop · Follow up
  5. MSC splits Oceania shipping into new loops MSC revised its Oceania network with a Northern Loop linking Sydney, Auckland, Napier and Tauranga and a separate Brisbane–Noumea–Lautoka–Suva loop; the Fiji service starts 8 September and the Northern Loop’s first Sydney call is scheduled for 12 September. 2 Sep 2026. Daily Cargo News · Follow up
  6. New Zealand’s Living Wage rises to $29.90 The voluntary 2026/27 New Zealand Living Wage took effect at NZ$29.90 an hour, up 95 cents from NZ$28.95; accredited employers were required to move covered staff to the new rate from 1 September. 1 Sep 2026. Calk NZ · Follow up
  7. Subaru prices the electric Trailseeker for New Zealand Subaru set New Zealand pricing for its new electric Trailseeker from NZ$68,990, adding a second variant; the model offers 280kW and up to 533km WLTP range, with local stock due from October. 2 Sep 2026. EVs & Beyond · Follow up
  8. Microsoft Entra starts pushing passkeys by default From 1 September, Microsoft Entra ID automatically enables passkeys for users currently enabled for SMS or voice MFA and prompts eligible users to register one; Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication is scheduled to retire on 1 February 2027. 1 Sep 2026. Microsoft Learn · Follow up
  9. Ethena Pay goes live in New Zealand Ethena Pay is now live in New Zealand as part of its initial 49-country rollout, offering eligible adults a self-custodial stablecoin account with transfers and card-related features; New Zealand is explicitly listed among supported jurisdictions. 1–2 Sep 2026. Ethena Pay · Follow up
  10. Chrome 152 ships security fixes Google released Chrome 152 stable updates carrying fixes for 26 security vulnerabilities, including multiple critical issues; no known active exploitation was reported at release, making an update the practical action for Chrome users. 2 Sep 2026. PC-WELT · Follow up
  11. Android’s September feature update begins rolling out Google began rolling out Android features including Motion Assist for motion-sickness reduction, Gemini-assisted Find Hub capabilities, expanded Guided Vision accessibility and Google Keep sharing inside Messages; availability varies by Android version and device. 1 Sep 2026. TechCrunch · Follow up
  12. Google launches Pics for AI image creation and editing Google launched Google Pics for eligible Workspace and Google AI subscribers, adding prompt-based image generation plus object-level edits, text changes and translation, upscaling and collaboration, with integration into Docs and Slides. 1–2 Sep 2026. The Verge · Follow up
  13. Malaysia Airlines restores Kuala Lumpur–Fukuoka flights Malaysia Airlines restarted direct Kuala Lumpur–Fukuoka service on 2 September after roughly 20 years, operating five weekly flights and adding another one-stop Japan option via Kuala Lumpur for New Zealand travellers. 2 Sep 2026. Airport Routes · Follow up
  14. Sonos unveils Beam Ultra and Ace Ultra Sonos introduced the Beam Ultra soundbar and Ace Ultra headphones, with pre-orders open from 1 September and general availability scheduled for 29 September; Beam Ultra adds 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos and Ace Ultra adds a new driver and next-generation adaptive noise cancellation. 1–2 Sep 2026. Sonos · Follow up
  15. SH2 Waioweka Gorge remains restricted after a slip State Highway 2 through Waioweka Gorge is down to one lane after a 30 August slip, with stop/stop closures of up to 10 minutes during daytime rock-scaling work on 2–3 September and stop/go traffic outside those periods. 1–2 Sep 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  16. Lower Hutt SH2 gets four nights of southbound closures State Highway 2 will close southbound between Kennedy Good Bridge and Melling Link Bridge from 9pm to 4am on 6–10 September for Melling project works; northbound traffic remains open and southbound traffic must detour locally. 2 Sep 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  17. Picasso exhibition confirmed for Auckland Auckland Art Gallery announced Picasso: Designed by Paul Smith, opening 10 October with more than 80 paintings, sculptures, ceramics, prints and drawings from the Musée national Picasso-Paris collection. 2 Sep 2026. Times · Follow up
  18. MOTAT announces a new Auckland transport exhibition MOTAT announced All Aboard – How Tāmaki Moves, an interactive exhibition on Auckland public-transport history, engineering and technology opening 26 September and running for a year, with objects, archives, projections, sound and interactive displays. 1 Sep 2026. Scoop · Follow up

item.title: Travel Rules Tighten While Costs and Connections Shift
item.description: Fresh travel rules, transport openings, price changes and practical service updates reshape several near-term choices.
item.content:encoded:
Fresh travel rules, transport openings, price changes and practical service updates reshape several near-term choices.

  1. Thailand cuts visa-free stays to 30 days Thailand published the final rule cutting visa-exempt tourism stays for New Zealanders and nationals of 59 other countries from 60 to 30 days from 15 September; the existing one-time 30-day extension remains available. 1 Sep 2026. Pattaya News · Follow up
  2. Europe’s EES biometric checks become fully enforced From 7 September, the EU Entry/Exit System becomes fully enforced across 29 European countries, ending temporary flexibility to pause biometric checks; first-time covered travellers register facial images, fingerprints and passport details. 1 Sep 2026. The Times · Follow up
  3. Australia’s major card networks ban merchant surcharges from October From 1 October, Visa, Mastercard, American Express and eftpos scheme rules will prohibit Australian merchants from adding surcharges to covered prepaid, debit and credit card payments; existing legal surcharge rules continue through 30 September. 31 Aug 2026. ACCC · Follow up
  4. Western Sydney Airport completes passenger-jet trial A Jetstar A320 landed at Western Sydney International on 1 September for an end-to-end passenger trial; the airport’s first commercial passenger flight is scheduled for 25 October, with Air New Zealand Auckland services starting the next day. 1 Sep 2026. Jetstar · Australian Government · Follow up
  5. Switch 2 jumps NZ$170 in New Zealand Nintendo’s Switch 2 console price rose from NZ$799.95 to NZ$969.95 on 1 September, a roughly 21% increase; Australia’s recommended price also rose from A$699.95 to A$769.95. 1 Sep 2026. GamesRadar · Follow up
  6. New Zealand Maersk inland fuel fee rises to 20% Maersk’s New Zealand Intermodal Fuel Fee moved to 20% from 1 September, replacing the lower March setting; the fee applies to covered landside and intermodal transport and is reviewed monthly. 1 Sep 2026. Maersk · Follow up
  7. Melton’s new railway station opens Victoria opened the new elevated Melton Station to passengers on 1 September with four platforms, lifts, an underpass and new rail bridges; longer nine-car VLocity trains are planned to stop there from 2027. 1 Sep 2026. Victoria · V/Line · Follow up
  8. Victoria starts a major spring transport-works period Victoria began a spring works program that includes Coburns Road closing 6–24 September, Maddox Road closing until 15 September, and the Eastern Freeway between Chandler Highway and Tram Road closing overnight across 11–14 September. 1 Sep 2026. Victoria · Follow up
  9. Australian supermarkets trial facial recognition Coles and Woolworths have trialled facial-recognition systems in Australian stores, scanning facial features into digital identifiers; neither retailer has announced a nationwide rollout. 1 Sep 2026. ABC · Follow up
  10. Woolworths proposes shifting NZ customer-care work to Sydney Woolworths New Zealand began consultation on integrating its customer-care operation with a Sydney-based group support team, putting more than 100 New Zealand roles at risk; the company says no final decision has been made. 1 Sep 2026. 1News · Follow up
  11. Flu vaccination becomes free for all NZ under-fives From 1 September, every New Zealand child aged six months up to their fifth birthday is eligible for a funded influenza vaccine; Pharmac says national stock is sufficient for the expanded eligibility. 1 Sep 2026. Pharmac · Follow up
  12. Australian basic postage rises to A$1.85 Australia Post’s Basic Postage Rate increased from A$1.70 to A$1.85 on 1 September; regular large-letter prices also rose, while concession and seasonal greeting-card stamp prices stayed unchanged. 1 Sep 2026. Australia Post · ACCC · Follow up
  13. Aurora Serverless gets faster in AWS New Zealand AWS made Aurora Serverless platform version 4 available in its New Zealand region with up to 30% better performance and enhanced scaling at no additional charge; new clusters, restores and clones use it automatically. 31 Aug 2026. AWS · Follow up
  14. AWS–Azure private interconnect enters Sydney preview AWS opened a public preview of managed private multicloud interconnection with Microsoft Azure in Sydney, allowing AWS–Azure connectivity to be provisioned through AWS without a do-it-yourself cross-cloud network. 31 Aug 2026. AWS · Follow up
  15. AWS Agent Registry reaches Sydney in general availability AWS made Agent Registry generally available in Sydney and four other regions, providing a private governed catalogue for agents, tools, skills and MCP servers with organisation-wide discovery and sharing. 31 Aug 2026. AWS · Follow up
  16. Lambda runaway-loop protection expands worldwide AWS expanded Lambda recursive-loop detection to every commercial AWS region; the default-on guardrail detects supported recursive invocation loops, stops processing and sends an AWS Health notification before usage keeps compounding. 31 Aug 2026. AWS · Follow up
  17. New Zealand ECE regulation moves to ERO Responsibility for regulating New Zealand early childhood education services moved to the Education Review Office on 1 September, creating a separate regulator from the Ministry of Education. 1 Sep 2026. New Zealand Government · Follow up
  18. Air New Zealand says engine disruption is easing Air New Zealand reported that more grounded aircraft are returning to service as engine availability improves, reducing the fleet disruption that had constrained capacity; the airline reported its annual result on 27 August. 27 Aug 2026. Reuters · Follow up

item.title: Travel, Privacy and Work Rules Shift
item.description: Fresh transport disruptions, privacy rules, work changes and practical service launches lead today’s briefing.
item.content:encoded:
Fresh transport disruptions, privacy rules, work changes and practical service launches create several concrete choices to act on now.

  1. SH6 Makarora–Lake Hāwea reopens only by escorted convoy NZTA will run up to three escorted convoy movements daily from 1 September through the slip-hit section of State Highway 6, which has been closed since Friday after about 30 slips; heavy rain may force another full closure. 31 Aug 2026. NZTA · Follow up
  2. Australia unveils a right to erase platform data Australia released draft privacy reforms that would let people require large social-media platforms and search engines to destroy their personal information, add a “fair and reasonable” data-use test, tighten consent rules, and create myGov IDLock testing later in 2026 before a 2027 rollout. 31 Aug 2026. ABC · Follow up
  3. Queensland now requires licences for e-bikes and e-scooters From 31 August, public riders of e-bikes, e-scooters, e-skateboards and e-unicycles in Queensland must generally be at least 16 and hold a valid learner licence or higher; equivalent overseas licences count, with specified supervision, recreation and medical exemptions. 31 Aug 2026. Queensland Government · Qld transport · Follow up
  4. Thailand tightens Destination Thailand Visa applications Thai missions have tightened DTV supporting documents from 31 August: the London embassy now requires permanent-residence proof in its jurisdiction instead of proof of current location, plus a criminal-record certificate issued within six months, materially reducing the convenience of applying while merely visiting a third country. 31 Aug 2026. Royal Thai Embassy London · DTV change summary · Follow up
  5. Victoria delays its proposed work-from-home right Victoria’s proposed legal right for eligible workers to work from home two days a week will not start on 1 September; Premier Ben Carroll moved the intended commencement to 1 July 2027 while the bill remains under parliamentary consideration. 11 Aug 2026. ABC · Follow up
  6. Melbourne shows concrete Microsoft Fabric hiring demand Multiple Melbourne employers are recruiting for hands-on Microsoft Fabric work: Kinetic is building a new ANZ enterprise data platform, More says it is mid-way through a shift to Fabric, and a global investment manager is offering a 12-month senior Fabric/Power BI data-engineering contract at A$950 a day including super. 20–31 Aug 2026. Kinetic role · More role · Profusion role · Follow up
  7. Australia sets minimum pay floors for app delivery work Australia’s first enforceable minimum-standards order for employee-like on-demand food and grocery delivery workers is now operating, with engaged-time floors of A$31.30 an hour for bicycle/e-scooter work, A$31.50 for motorcycle work and A$32 for car or small-van work, plus required top-ups when earnings fall short. 17 Aug 2026. Fair Work Ombudsman · Follow up
  8. Ring makes stronger video encryption the worldwide default Ring’s new TAKE encryption will roll out in phases from September and become the default for all customers worldwide; each video uses rotating keys that Ring can access temporarily inside a secure enclave for enabled cloud features before the keys are deleted, while end-to-end encryption remains optional. 27 Aug 2026. Amazon · Ring NZ · Follow up
  9. Auckland City Rail Link starts passenger service 13 September Auckland Transport has published first-service details for the completed City Rail Link: passenger trains begin around 5am on Sunday 13 September, with new underground stations and through-running that cuts Panmure–Karanga-a-Hape to about 21 minutes and Glen Innes–Te Waihorotiu to about 15 minutes. 27 Aug 2026. Auckland Transport · CRL · Follow up
  10. New Zealand runway-end safety rules take effect New Civil Aviation Rules took effect on 31 August, aligning runway-end safety-area requirements with ICAO standards and allowing engineered arresting systems; CAA says the change gives regional airports more flexibility and can enable larger passenger aircraft where runway geometry previously constrained development. 31 Aug 2026. CAA · CAA summary · Follow up
  11. Sunbury trains face an open-ended replacement-bus disruption From 1 September, buses replace trains between Watergardens and Sunbury until further notice because of industrial action; services between Watergardens and central Melbourne will run to an altered timetable. 30 Aug 2026. Transport Victoria · Follow up
  12. Google releases Gemini 3.5 Transcribe Google released Gemini 3.5 Transcribe with real-time and recorded-audio transcription, automatic formatting and filler-word cleanup, custom vocabulary, automatic language detection across more than 85 languages, speaker attribution for up to three speakers and word-level timestamps; developers can access it through Gemini APIs. 26 Aug 2026. Google · DeepMind · Follow up
  13. Ask Gemini begins rolling out inside Google Chat Google began a gradual rollout of Ask Gemini in Chat for eligible Workspace plans on 26 August, adding one interface that can search Gmail, Drive and Calendar, catch up conversations, create content, and manage meetings and tasks without leaving Chat. 26 Aug 2026. Google Workspace · Follow up
  14. Star Wars Zero Company is now available EA released the turn-based tactics game Star Wars Zero Company on 27 August; Steam currently shows a Mostly Positive user consensus with about 78% positive English-language reviews, clearing the briefing’s review-quality threshold for a major Star Wars release. 27 Aug 2026. Steam · Follow up
  15. Auckland ferry terminal changes start 1 September Pier 2 at Auckland’s Downtown Ferry Terminal will close from 1 September to early November for electric-ferry charging works, moving Devonport services to Pier 4; a nearby Queens Wharf footpath section will also close until early December. 24 Aug 2026. Auckland Transport · Follow up
  16. Christchurch launches an Aranui–New Brighton trial bus Metro Christchurch started Route 110 on 31 August, running hourly between New Brighton and The Palms via Aranui, Pak’nSave Breezes Road and Burwood Park; the trial is scheduled for 12 months and accepts contactless cards, Metrocard and cash. 31 Aug 2026. Metro Christchurch · Follow up
  17. Kmart’s biggest New Zealand store opens 10 September Kmart will open a 6,700-square-metre, 24-hour Westgate store in Auckland on 10 September, its largest New Zealand location and the country’s first using the retailer’s Plan C+ format. 19 Aug 2026. Inside Retail NZ · Follow up
  18. Tupperware returns to New Zealand after four years Tupperware relaunched in New Zealand on 24 August after ceasing local trading in 2022, with a new local distributor and a full-range e-commerce store; retail partnerships are planned later. 24–25 Aug 2026. Inside Retail NZ · Idealog · Follow up
